$comment: The agent's tools: names, descriptions and JSON Schema.
Data rather than code because two implementations read it, and because the
descriptions are prompt engineering. 'Needs a date: with none given and none
saved on the trip, it returns a request to ask the traveller rather than
pricing a week nobody chose' is a behaviour, written down. Retyping that into
a second language is how two agents end up with different manners.

tools.name: search_flights
tools.description: Finds flights to a destination. Returns fare, timing and stop data — not UI. Call it before showing flight options so the numbers on screen are real. Needs a date: with none given and none saved on the trip, it returns a request to ask the traveler rather than pricing a week nobody chose. Set flexible only when they explicitly asked for a rough or seasonal figure.

destination.description: Where the traveler is going: a city name or airport code, e.g. 'Madrid' or 'MAD'.

origin.description: Departure airport code. Required — the trip is not priced without one.

flexible.description: Only when the traveler asked for a rough or seasonal figure rather than their trip. Prices an indicative date, which you must then label as indicative on screen.

draw.description: What to put on screen *while this runs*, so the traveler watches an interface fill in rather than waiting at an empty space. The list is drawn the moment the lookup starts and the rows land in it when they come back. Omit it only if you are drawing something else yourself.

heading.description: One line above the list, e.g. 'Outbound · JFK → MAD · Sun 12 Apr'.

selected.description: Data path holding the current choice, e.g. '/trip/selectedOutbound', so the chosen card stays marked.

hop.description: Which hop these are for, when it is not the first — hop two is '/legs/0'. The press carries it so the choice lands on that leg.

tools.name: search_hotels
tools.description: Finds places to stay. Returns nightly rates, neighbourhoods, ratings and amenities — not UI.

neighborhood.description: Preferred area, if the traveler named one.

flexible.description: Only for an explicitly rough figure. See search_flights.

draw.description: What to put on screen *while this runs*, so the traveler watches an interface fill in rather than waiting at an empty space. The list is drawn the moment the lookup starts and the rows land in it when they come back. Omit it only if you are drawing something else yourself.

heading.description: One line above the list, e.g. 'Outbound · JFK → MAD · Sun 12 Apr'.

selected.description: Data path holding the current choice, e.g. '/trip/selectedOutbound', so the chosen card stays marked.

hop.description: Which hop these are for, when it is not the first — hop two is '/legs/0'. The press carries it so the choice lands on that leg.

tools.name: get_destination
tools.description: Returns what is worth doing in a destination, when to go, and the local currency. Call it before writing an itinerary so the day plan names real places. With no argument, lists every destination this agent knows.

destination.description: City name or airport code. Omit to list all.

draw.description: What to put on screen *while this runs*. The highlights are drawn the moment the lookup starts and land in the list when they come back. Worth passing on any planning turn: writing the day plan into save_trip is the longest thing you say, and nothing about the plan exists to promise until it is written, so without this the traveler waits at an empty space for all of it.

heading.description: One line above the list, e.g. 'Worth your time in Berlin'.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description: Returns a short forecast for a destination — highs, lows and conditions by day.

startDate.description: First day of the forecast, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: Breaks a trip into itemised costs and a total. Pass the chosen fare and nightly rate when the traveler has picked them, so the estimate reflects their actual trip rather than an average. Needs dates and party size, from the arguments or the saved trip; without them it returns a request to ask instead of a total that means nothing.

flexible.description: Only for an explicitly rough figure. See search_flights.

tools.name: save_trip
tools.description: Records what the traveler has decided. Anything not saved here is forgotten when the turn ends. Returns what is still needed.

origin.description: Departure airport code for the first hop — 'SFO'. Later hops carry their own on the leg.

spent.description: What is actually committed, not estimated.

days.description: The day-by-day plan itself, one entry per day, in order — not just the fact that you drew one. Save it in the same call that draws it: the itinerary on the card cannot be shared, edited or read back next turn, and a hop whose days are not recorded goes on asking for things to do after you have planned them.

title.description: What this day is, e.g. 'Old Madrid on foot'.

summary.description: One line about the shape of the day.

planned.description: True once the day-by-day plan is drawn and the traveler is happy with it.

skip.description: Stages this trip does not need. A skipped stage counts as settled.

assumed.description: Fields in this call the traveler did not actually state — your best guess rather than their answer. They pre-fill the control and the question stays open, so you still ask.

oneWay.description: True when the journey does not come back — one way, staying on, sorting the way home later. Record it and stop looking for the missing hop home.

legs.description: Stops after the first, in order. The top-level fields are the first leg.

origin.description: Departure airport. Omit and it departs from the previous stop.

travelers.description: Only when this leg differs. Omit and it inherits the trip's.

needsStay.description: Whether this stop needs somewhere to stay.

selectedFlight.description: The flight chosen for this hop. Every hop after the first keeps its own ticket here — the trip's `selectedFlight` is the first hop's and nothing else.

flightPrice.description: Per-traveler fare of that hop's flight.

selectedHotel.description: The stay chosen for this stop.

airline.description: This hop's. Who flies it, off the card they tapped — 'Norwegian'.

departTime.description: This hop's. When it leaves, as the card showed it — '07:15'.

arriveTime.description: This hop's. When it lands, as the card showed it — '11:40'.

hotelName.description: This hop's. What the stay is called, off the card they tapped.

notes.description: Anything else worth remembering, in one line.

needsStay.description: Whether the first stop needs somewhere to stay. False when they already have somewhere. Later stops carry this on their leg.

draw.description: The card to put on screen the moment this call lands, so it costs no further round. Send it on every turn that records something and then shows something — which is most of them. Drawing the same card in a block of your own afterwards is correct and spends an entire extra round on it. The result will tell you it is up; say one sentence and end the turn.

macro.description: `Ask` for the form of what is still missing — the answer on almost every turn before the flights are priced. `Itinerary` for the day plan, when this call carried `days`.

heading.description: One line above it, e.g. 'Madrid in April' or 'Four days in Berlin'.

label.description: `Ask` only: what the button says. Defaults to 'Find flights'.

airline.description: Who flies it, off the card they tapped — 'Norwegian'. Save it with the id: the panel says what the flight *is*, and it can only read what you recorded.

departTime.description: When it leaves, as the card showed it — '07:15'.

arriveTime.description: When it lands, as the card showed it — '11:40'.

hotelName.description: What the stay is called, off the card they tapped. `selectedHotel` is an id; this is the name a person reads.

maxFare.description: Highest acceptable per-traveler fare, when they named a ceiling.

maxNightly.description: Highest acceptable nightly rate, when they named one.

tools.name: release_decision
tools.description: Lets go of something already decided. Clears the named fields *and* what depended on them, and returns what it cleared.

fields.description: Trip fields to release, e.g. ['startDate'] or ['selectedFlight'].

tools.name: get_trip
tools.description: Reads back everything recorded about this trip so far.

tools.name: share_plan
tools.description: Turns the trip into a page somebody who is not in this conversation can read: the route hop by hop, where you are staying, the days, and what it comes to. Call it when the trip is settled and they want to send it to whoever else is coming. Returns the page as Markdown plus a one-line summary — not a surface; draw a Button beside it if they should be able to open it again.

note.description: One line at the top, in the traveller's own framing — 'Lisbon, the weekend of the 12th'. Optional.
